methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $5M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $1.8B.

data.narrative:
Orangewood Labs is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $5M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of nine private companies and one public equity in the robotics sector, including later-stage peers Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B Series B), and earlier-stage Walden Robotics ($1.1B Seed).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $5M total raised as a baseline proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement to the next milestone, yielding $10M. Peer-median analysis references three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with a median valuation of $1.6B and a range of $1.1B to $1.8B.

The wide dispersion between methods reflects the challenge of benchmarking an early-stage company against substantially more mature peers. The stage-progression method is mechanically sound but treats the company in isolation; the peer approach anchors to observable market pricing but suffers from stage mismatch—the comparable set skews toward Series B and later. A reasonable valuation range is $8M to $1.9B, with a triangulated median of $830M. The analysis is heavily sensitive to whether Orangewood's progression trajectory and market timing align with peer benchmarks. Further work should clarify revenue or traction metrics relative to comps at their respective Series A stages.
